channel.title: MIND / MATTER Daily Briefing
channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: Objective To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

item.title: Hardware Demonstration of Neural-Surrogated Quantum-Enhanced MCMC for Large-Scale Constrained Boltzmann Sampling
item.description: Neural-surrogated quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo (QeMCMC) uses neural networks trained on samples from the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to accelerate Boltzmann sampling. A divide-and-conquer strategy extends this approach to larger systems, but independently optimizing QAOA parameters for each subproblem is costly.

item.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
item.description: Abstract Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

item.title: The Association Between Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Postoperative Delirium: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description: Background: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication following surgery, particularly in high-risk patients such as those with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The relationship between COPD and the development of POD remains unclear, with existing studies providing inconsistent findings.

item.title: Digital engineering for quantum communication networks: A systematic review of models, simulators, and testbeds
item.description: Research on quantum communication networks has grown rapidly in recent years, driven by progress in quantum devices, simulators, and experimental testbeds. As these systems become more complex, there is increasing interest in digital methods that can support analysis, prediction, and performance assessment without relying exclusively on physical experimentation.

item.title: Quantum Computing for Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Field Theory
item.description: We construct a quantum measurement protocol for estimating the Rényi entanglement asymmetry, which quantifies symmetry breaking at the level of a subsystem and provides a probe of the quantum Mpemba effect. The protocol combines the SWAP test with a charge-resolving procedure based on randomized symmetry rotations.

item.title: Discovering correlated error mechanisms: data-driven augmentation of detector error models improving decoding
item.description: Accurate decoder priors are essential for high-performance quantum error correction. Theoretical noise models inevitably omit physically relevant error mechanisms, most notably correlated errors, which appear consistently in experimental error budgets yet are absent from standard models.

item.title: Thermodynamics-Informed Learning Captures Hierarchical Hydrogen-Bond Networks in Deep Eutectic Solvents
item.description: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) offer a tunable platform for lignocellulose refining, but their solvation behavior depends on multicomponent hydrogen-bond networks rather than individual constituent properties. We develop TiNN, a thermodynamics-informed neural network that hierarchically represents HBA-HBD association and solute accommodation through a learned free-energy pathway.

item.title: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy
item.description: This paper investigates Lorentz violation arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The violation is modeled through a modified dispersion relation parameterized by a dimensionless coefficient $ξ$ and suppressed by the Planck scale.

item.title: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation
item.description: Driven-dissipative polariton networks offer a powerful analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. However, their practical scalability is fundamentally limited by amplitude-phase coupling and metastable trapping in highly frustrated energy landscapes.

item.title: Time-Division Multiplexing: The Operational Rhythm and Temporal Organization Layer of Digital Life
item.description: Continual agents must handle urgent interaction while retaining alternatives, replaying errors, and committing safe long-term changes. A previous digital-life framework distinguishes online (busy) and offline (idle) channels, but leaves open whether these are separate programs or phases of a common process and how their operations should be ordered.

item.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
item.description: Abstract The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, and fragility of quantum states under measurement. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet.

item.title: Common phenomenal and neural substrate geometry in visual motion perception
item.description: Abstract What is a possible physical substrate of the qualitative aspects of consciousness (qualia)? Answering this question is a central goal of consciousness research. Due to their subjective and ineffable nature, finding a quantitative way to characterise qualia from verbal description has thus far proven elusive.

item.title: Quantum machine learning for quantitative finance
item.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) and quantum ML (QML) have gained significant importance, as they offer powerful tools for tackling complex computational problems across various domains. An overview of QML’s uses in quantitative finance is presented here.

item.title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
item.description: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations.

item.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
item.description: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location.

item.title: The Spontaneous Disentanglement Hypothesis and Causality
item.description: ABSTRACT The hypothesis that disentanglement spontaneously occurs in quantum systems is motivated by some outstanding issues in the foundations of quantum mechanics. However, for some cases, spontaneous disentanglement enables the violation of the causality principle.
